layout_dets.text: Ridge-Based Vessel Segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in Color Images of the Retina

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Joes Staal*, Associate Member, IEEE, Michael D. Abràmoff, Member, IEEE, Meindert Niemeijer,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Max A. Viergever, Member, IEEE, and Bram van Ginneken, Associate Member, IEEE

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Abstract—A method is presented for automated segmentation of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vessels in two-dimensional color images of the retina. This method

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: can be used in computer analyses of retinal images, e.g., in au-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tomated screening for diabetic retinopathy. The system is based

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on extraction of image ridges, which coincide approximately with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vessel centerlines. The ridges are used to compose primitives in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: form of line elements. With the line elements an image is parti-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tioned into patches by assigning each image pixel to the closest line

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: element. Every line element constitutes a local coordinate frame

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for its corresponding patch. For every pixel, feature vectors are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: computed that make use of properties of the patches and the line

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: elements. The feature vectors are classified using a kNN-classi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fier and sequential forward feature selection. The algorithm was

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tested on a database consisting of 40 manually labeled images. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: method achieves an area under the receiver operating character-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: istic curve of 0.952. The method is compared with two recently pub-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lished rule-based methods of Hoover et al. [1] and Jiang et al. [2].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The results show that our method is significantly better than the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: two rule-based methods

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: . The accuracy of our method

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is 0.944 versus 0.947 for a second observer.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fundus, image primitives, retina, ridges, vessel segmentation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: I. INTRODUCTION

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SSESSMENT of the characteristics of vessels plays an

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: important role in a variety of medical diagnoses. For these

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tasks measurements are needed of e.g., vessel width, color

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reflectivity, tortuosity, abnormal branching, or the occurrence

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of vessels of a certain width. When the number of vessels in an

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: image is large, or when a large number of images is acquired,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: manual delineation of the vessels becomes tedious or even

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: impossible.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The focus of this paper is on the automated segmentation of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vessels in color images of the retina. These images, also known

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as fundus images, are acquired by making photographs of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: back of the eye. We are interested in vessel segmentation for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: screening of diabetic retinopathy. Diabetes is a disease that af-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fects about 5.5% of the population worldwide, a number that can

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: be expected to increase significantly in the coming years. About

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 10% of all diabetic patients have diabetic retinopathy, which is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the primary cause of blindness in the Western World. Since this

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: type of blindness can be prevented with treatment at an early

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: stage, the WHO advises yearly ocular screening of patients. Au-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tomation will facilitate this screening [3].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Knowledge about the location of the vessels can aid in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: screening of diabetic retinopathy, e.g., to reduce the number of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: false positives in the detection of microaneurysms [4]–[6], to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: serve as a means for registration of images taken at different

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: time instants or at different locations of the retina [7], or to find

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the location of the optic disc and the fovea.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Previous methods for vessel segmentation in images of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the retina can be divided into two groups. The first group

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: consists of rule-based methods and comprises vessel tracking

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: [8]–[11], matched filter responses [1], [12], [13], grouping of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: edge pixels [14], model based locally adaptive thresholding

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: [2], topology adaptive snakes [15] and morphology-based

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: techniques [16]–[18]. The second group consists of supervised

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: methods, which require manually labeled images for training.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To the best of our knowledge, the only published method in this

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: category is the neural network scheme for pixel classification

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by Sinthanayothin et al. [19], [20]. Our method belongs to the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: last category.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In our opinion, a pixel representation is not optimal for vessel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: structure. Therefore, our approach is based on the intrinsic prop-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: erty that vessels are elongated structures. This observation leads

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to a primitive-based method, which we refer to as PBM. Our al-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: gorithm uses image primitives formed from image ridges that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are grouped into sets that approximate straight line elements.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The sets are used for two purposes. First, features are computed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which together with a classifier give a probability that the line

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: element is part of a vessel. Second, the sets divide the image

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: into patches by assigning every pixel of the image to its nearest

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: primitive. Within each patch, the line element defines a local co-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ordinate frame in which local features can be extracted for every

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pixel. The probability that the line element is part of a vessel is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: one of these features. The features are used to classify the pixels

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in the patch into vessel and nonvessel.

layout_dets.text: II. REPRESENTATION OF VESSELS

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: A. Ridge Detection

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Since image ridges are natural indicators of vessels, we start

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: our analysis with a short overview of ridge detection for two-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dimensional gray value images. For a more extensive discussion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on this subject, see [21] and [22]. The ridge detection method

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: used in this paper is described in full detail in [22]. Because

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the green channel of color fundus images formatted as an RGB

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: image gives the highest contrast between vessel and background

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: [1], this channel is used for extraction of the image ridges.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Ridges are defined as points where the image has an ex-

layout_dets.text: B. Affine Convex Sets: Grouping Ridge Pixels

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The next step in forming primitives for the vessels is a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: grouping of ridge pixels which belong to the same ridge. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: aim is to obtain primitives which represent approximately

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: straight line elements.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The grouping method is a simple region growing algorithm

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which compares an already grouped ridge pixel with ungrouped

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pixels in a neighborhood of radius

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: one is selected randomly as seed from the remaining ungrouped

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ridge pixels. The comparison between the grouped and a candi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: date pixel within the neighborhood is based on two conditions:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1) The eigenvector directions of the ridge pixels should be sim-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: same ridge (and not on parallel ridges). The first condition can

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.text: III. FEATURES AND CLASSIFIERS

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The goal of this work is to classify every pixel in an image

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as vessel or nonvessel. For this purpose labeled examples or

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: training sets, features and a classifier are needed.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: From the training sets feature vectors are constructed that can

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: be labeled as vessel or nonvessel, so every feature vector belongs

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to one of two classes. The idea is that feature vectors from a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: particular class cluster together in the feature space and that a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: classifier can be designed that determines a decision boundary

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: between the different classes. After the training, a nonlabeled

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: feature vector can be classified by determining on which side

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the decision boundary it is situated. With some classifiers it

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is possible to approximate the chance, given the features, that a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pixel is vessel or not. This is called soft classification.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: A. Classification and Performance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: implementation for kNN-classifiers that is made available by

layout_dets.text: B. Feature Selection

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In the following sections, many features will be defined and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: it is not known beforehand which ones will give good classifi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cation results and which ones will not. Therefore, feature selec-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion is applied. The scheme used in this paper is the sequential

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: forward selection method [28]. This algorithm starts with a null

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: have been included, the set that gives the best performance is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: chosen.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: A perfect system would yield

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: , which is not reached

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by our method. There are a few reasons. First, in all images high

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: probability for being vessel is found around the boundaries of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the FOV, while there are no vessels; see Fig. 6(a) and (e) for an

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: example. This is an artifact of the method, introduced by the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: blurring that is needed for detecting the ridges of the image.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Second, in some images part of the boundary of the optic disc

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is marked as vessel, cf. Fig. 6(a), while a human observer can

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: clearly discern between the two. This is an indication that the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: amount of training data might be insufficient. Third, related to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the last observation, is the appearance of (severe) pathology

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of which Fig. 8 gives an example. The method selects with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: high probability some vessels between bright areas where there

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are clearly no vessels. More training data that includes the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: various types of pathology encountered in screening practice

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: might overcome this problem. No experiments were done to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: investigate the influence of the amount of training data. However,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: certain types of pathology might be detected and labeled in a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: preprocessing step. A fourth reason for imperfect performance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the method can be the incorrect labeling of the convex

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sets in the training sets. Or even worse, no ridge is detected

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: at the location of a vessel, which can happen for very small

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vessels. This can occur because the locations of the ridges are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: perturbed by the blurring that is needed for their detection.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: For large vessels, the detected ridge pixels are still within the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vessel, but for small vessels they can be a little off. A possible

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: solution might be to do ridge detection with scale selection,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: like in [24]. Another interesting reason for scale selection is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the use of scale as a feature.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: For the PBM it takes about 15 min to segment an image in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Utrecht database on a Pentium-III PC, running at 1.0 GHz with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1-GB memory. Most time is spent in the classification. However,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: our implementation is experimental and could be optimized. For

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: example, Table II shows that for both databases, the most impor-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tant feature is the probability that a convex set is part of a vessel.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: It can be expected that for a set with low probability of being

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vessel the pixels in its CSR will have low probability. This mea-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sure can be used to speed up the segmentation by not processing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: CSR belonging to convex sets with a low chance of being vessel.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In the Utrecht database, we observed that only about 10% of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: convex sets have a probability higher than 0.5. In [2], processing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: times of about half a minute are reported. Computation times for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: [1] are not available.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In this paper, evaluation has been done using accuracy of hard

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: classifications and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: values of soft classifications. Other evalu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ation measures might be more appropriate, depending on the ap-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: plication at hand. For example, if one is interested in examining

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the tortuosity of the vessels, the width of the vessels might not be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: important, only the centerlines. The measures used do not take

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: into account the number of branches, the connectedness of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vessels or the number of branching points, which all might be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: relevant in specific applications. Another good evaluation mea-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sure might be the performance of a computer-aided diagnosis

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: system for retinal images that uses the results of a vessel seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentation algorithm in its analysis.
